injection_levels.provider_level: Provider or model configuration attached outside the task body.
injection_levels.session_level: Attached to a whole Hermes session or model provider configuration.
injection_levels.request_level: Attached to one model request body.
injection_levels.content_block_level: Attached to a system, message, tool, or content block.
injection_levels.cache_entry_level: Attached to a cache-control breakpoint or provider cache entry.
injection_levels.runtime_feedback_level: Reported after provider execution as usage or metrics feedback.

source_classes.provider_config: A Hermes provider, request_overrides, or extra_body setting caused or carried the hint.
source_classes.prompt_builder_policy: Hermes placed cache-control metadata on stable prompt or skill blocks.
source_classes.provider_automatic: The provider derives the behavior without a client-visible field.
source_classes.pass_through: Hermes preserved configured request metadata at the request boundary.
source_classes.metrics_feedback: The value appears after execution as usage or metrics feedback.

hints.meaning: Carries provider-specific service tier or speed options through Hermes provider config or request overrides.
Hermes/provider cache reuse is based on prompt tiers and model identity, not necessarily a literal request cache key.
Hermes cache isolation is provider/session/model scoped; a literal namespace may only appear as configured gateway metadata.
Hermes prompt caching can request default 5m behavior or 1h retention where provider support exists.
Hermes prompt caching uses Anthropic-style ephemeral cache-control markers where supported.
Cache feedback is expected as provider usage or prompt-cache metrics after execution.
hints.supported_consumer: Benchmark report and cache validation tooling

hints.meaning: Hermes exposes provider retention windows such as 1h where supported, not a separate pin flag.
